summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV (CD4 count 14), end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of herpes zoster ophthalmicus presented with worsening right facial pain, new blistering skin lesions, and headaches. Initially suspected of zoster reactivation, she was admitted for evaluation and started on IV acyclovir. Workup including CT head, MRI, and lumbar puncture showed no evidence of central nervous system infection. Skin biopsies revealed eosinophilic folliculitis, not shingles, leading to discontinuation of acyclovir. The rash improved with mupirocin and hydroxyzine. Her headaches, though persistent, were deemed non-life-threatening. She remained stable on HAART and prophylactic medications, completed dialysis sessions without issue, and was discharged home with improved symptoms and follow-up plans.
problems: Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications
Other specified diseases of hair and hair follicles
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
